intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the TBPL2 gene (608964) on chromosome 14q22.3.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the TBPL2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous splicing variant (c.788 + 3A>G) in TBPL2 was identified in two unrelated families characterized by oocyte maturation defects.
checks.explanation: The paper reports only homozygous mutation. It does not mention compound heterozygous mutations or the OZEMA29 designation.

checks.claim: The TBPL2 gene is located on chromosome 14q22.3.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous splicing variant (c.788 + 3A>G) in TATA-box binding protein like 2 (TBPL2) was identified as a contributory genetic factor in oocyte maturation defects.
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature for the TBPL2 gene that the paper discusses.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29) is a form of female infertility. Reported features include oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration, with only immature metaphase I oocytes or no oocytes retrieved at in vitro fertilization (IVF). Some patients have impaired ovarian folliculogenesis and fail to respond to superovulation (Yang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021; Du et al., 2023).

checks.claim: OZEMA29 is a form of female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous variant in TBPL2 was identified in women with oocyte maturation defects and infertility.
checks.explanation: The paper describes female infertility caused by oocyte maturation defects.

checks.claim: Reported features of OZEMA29 include oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: two infertile sisters with oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration
checks.explanation: The paper reports oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration in the affected sisters.

checks.claim: In OZEMA29, only immature metaphase I oocytes or no oocytes are retrieved at in vitro fertilization.
checks.evidence_quote: Owing to the scarcity of human oocyte samples, only two immature MI oocytes were obtained from the patients
checks.explanation: The abstract supports retrieval of only MI oocytes. It does not mention cases where no oocytes were retrieved.

checks.claim: Some patients with OZEMA29 have impaired ovarian folliculogenesis and fail to respond to superovulation.
checks.evidence_quote: Compound heterozygous mutations in TBPL2 may be the cause of impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, failure of superovulation, and infertility.
checks.explanation: The paper states both impaired folliculogenesis and failure of superovulation.

paragraphs.text: In the Finnish population, Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that women homozygous for the TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter variant had significantly fewer offspring than women with other genotypes, an average of 0.16 compared with 1.75 (p = 1.4 x 10(-15)). Of 41 homozygous women, only 4 had given birth. All 4 had undergone IVF, and it was not known whether donor oocytes had been used. The authors concluded that the variant is associated with a fairly severe form of infertility.

paragraphs.text: OZEMA29 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. Yang et al. (2021) found homozygous TBPL2 mutations in affected women from 2 unrelated families, and Wang et al. (2021) found them in 2 affected sisters from a consanguineous family. Du et al. (2023) found compound heterozygous TBPL2 mutations in an affected woman. In a population-based study, Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that the TBPL2 locus acts recessively: the proportion of infertile women was significantly increased only among those carrying 2 copies of the effect allele. The association was seen equally in early-onset and late-onset infertility.

paragraphs.text: Du et al. (2023) performed whole-exome sequencing in a woman with primary infertility, impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, and failed superovulation, and confirmed the results in her family by Sanger sequencing. They identified compound heterozygous mutations in the TBPL2 gene. One was a novel nonsense mutation, c.802C-T, resulting in an arg268-to-ter (R268X) substitution. paragraphs.text: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) performed a genomewide association study in the Finnish FinnGen cohort, comparing 22,849 women with infertility with 198,989 control women who had given birth. Under a recessive model, they found a genome-wide significant association with a stop-gained variant in the TBPL2 gene, rs144313315 (c.895A-T, NM_199047.3), resulting in an arg299-to-ter (R299X) substitution (odds ratio, 650.1; p = 4.11 x 10(-25)). The variant introduces a premature stop codon in the DNA-binding part of the protein and was predicted to cause loss of function (CADD score, 40). It was associated with infertility only and with no other diseases.

checks.evidence_quote: The strongest association was observed in the recessive analysis at the TBPL2 locus on chromosome 14 with an odds ratio (OR) of 650.1 (p = 4.11 × 10−25). The lead variant in this locus, rs144313315 (c.895A>T [GenBank: NM_199047.3]), is a rare stop-gained mutation (p.Arg299Ter

checks.claim: TBPL2 R299X introduces a premature stop codon in the DNA-binding part of the protein.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation introduces a premature stop codon (p.Arg299Ter) in the DNA-binding part of the protein

checks.claim: TBPL2 R299X was predicted to cause loss of function (CADD score 40).
checks.evidence_quote: predicted to be a high-confidence predicted loss-of-function variant (pLOF) with a Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) score of 40

checks.claim: Women homozygous for TBPL2 R299X had an average of 0.16 offspring vs 1.75 in other genotype groups (p = 1.4 x 10(-15)).
checks.evidence_quote: individuals carrying two copies of that variant having significantly fewer offspring (average of 0.16) compared to women belonging to the other genotype groups (average of 1.75 offspring, p = 1.4 × 10-15)

checks.claim: Of 41 women homozygous for TBPL2 R299X, only 4 had given birth, all after IVF.
checks.evidence_quote: two out of 41 individuals carrying two copies of the risk allele had given birth to one child, whereas two individuals carrying two copies of the risk allele had given birth to more than one child. All four women had undergone IVF therapy

checks.claim: TBPL2 R299X has a minor allele frequency of 1.1% in Finland, 43 times higher than in non-Finnish Europeans.
checks.evidence_quote: is a rare stop-gained mutation (p.Arg299Ter, minor-allele frequency [MAF]: 1.1% in Finland) that is highly enriched to Finland (43 times compared to non-Finnish Europeans)
